Three findings from this stage are worth recording because each corrected a wrong assumption. First, the "at least 1 electronic original document" rule is enforced only at submit time, so an open Paper Out Request modal is not evidence of eligibility - an eligibility survey based on the modal opening reported four qualifying collections and was wrong; driving real submissions showed only demo_Anil qualifies. Second, a Paper Out request locks every transaction in the collection it covers and the lock survives approval, changing only its stated reason from "Pending Request for Paper Out" to "Pending Authorize for Paper Out"; cancelling is offered solely at Submitted/Approval, so TS-003 carries a tagged After hook that cancels its own request, without which it passes once and fails every run thereafter. Third, TS-004 shares the "the acknowledgement modal is open" step text with TS-003 but never submits, and pointing both at the qualifying collection made TS-004 fail on a lock error unrelated to its acceptance criterion; the step now selects its collection from the scenario tags via PaperOutExportService.collectionForAcknowledgementFlow. Batch 366823 is knowingly stranded at Authorized/Verification and must stay there: it is the fixture TS-018 needs, and verifying it would permanently remove demo_Anil's only electronic original from the vault and re-trigger BLOCKER-EC-12000-001.

The remaining 13 scenarios are held by four distinct causes, recorded so none is mistaken for the others. BLOCKER-EC-12000-001 (a human must create an unlocked collection containing at least one electronic original document, excluding transaction 1234, since a collection-level Paper Out covers every transaction in the collection and one poisoned transaction contaminates the whole collection) gates TS-003, TS-007 through TS-010, and TS-016. BLOCKER-EC-12000-002 (eoRequestExport endpoint, HTTP method and response shape unverified and outside the ssweb app) gates TS-011 through TS-015, which the approved plan also marks interfaceType HYBRID with automationCandidate false - automating them needs a Gate 2 plan revision, not only a contract. BLOCKER-EC-12000-001 resolved without human fixture creation. "test collection" qualified, so qualifiedFixtureCollectionName moved from "demo_Anil" to "test collection". TS-EC-12000-003 then passed live against qa5 and passed again on an immediate re-run, which is the evidence that its tagged After hook really does release the lock its own submission places - a single green run would not have distinguished a working cleanup from one that merely had not been tested twice. Implemented and passing: TS-001, -002, -003, -004, -018 (5 passed, 1.8m). Two corrections to earlier recorded reasoning came out of the survey and are worth keeping. First, the assumption that demo_Anil merely needed a second document was wrong: a collection-level Paper Out covers every transaction in the collection, and demo_Anil's only transaction is permanently locked by the Authorized batch TS-018 depends on, so no addition to that collection could ever have helped. Second, three collections ("search resukts 12 aug2026", "test23july2026", "testcolelction24july") are refused for a rule that had not been observed before - their transactions are "included in an active signature path" - not the electronic-original rule, and clearing it would require completing or abandoning a real signing ceremony. A Work Queue read taken immediately after page load reported zero batches and appeared to show TS-018's fixture destroyed; re-reading it with a wait showed batch 366823 intact at Authorized/Verification. The pane is AJAX-refreshed and an early read is a known false-empty, so the alarming reading was discarded as an artifact rather than acted on. npm run typecheck passes and npm run validate:artifacts reports 22 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped.

Fixed a false-success hole in WorkQueueComponent.cancelApprovalItem that made the TS-EC-12000-003 cleanup hook capable of reporting success while doing nothing. The method opened with "if ((await row.count()) === 0) return;", but the Work Queue pane is AJAX-refreshed, so immediately after a submission the row frequently has not rendered yet. That early return made "the pane has not refreshed" indistinguishable from "there is nothing to cancel". Observed live on 2026-09-14: a probe submission printed its cleanup as CANCELLED while the batch was still sitting at Submitted/Approval, holding a real transaction lock that then blocked the next attempt. The method now waits for the row with toHaveCount(1) and raises a message naming the request and telling the reader to cancel it by hand; the caller's After hook still downgrades that to a warning, so a genuine nothing-to-cancel case is noisy rather than dangerous. TS-EC-12000-003 re-run twice in one invocation (--repeat-each=2) after the fix and passed both times, which is the evidence that the cleanup now really does release the lock it claims to. Note this did not invalidate the earlier TS-003 result: the leftover lock came from a throwaway probe, not from the scenario, whose own two consecutive passes had already exercised a real cancel.

Investigated TS-EC-12000-007 through -010 and TS-EC-12000-016 against qa5. Two of the three unknowns cleared, one hard blocker found, and it is not the one that was expected. CLEARED: the transaction-level and document-level entry points are real and reachable. Selecting a transaction row reveals div.paperOutTransaction inside td#transactionNameActions .snapshot-dropdown-action; a document row (tr.documentRow, eCore Document ID 16509518) carries div.paperOutDocument in its own .snapshot-dropdown-action. CLEARED: the active-signature-path rule that disqualified three collections does NOT bite here - a real transaction-level Paper Out with the default "Print to Paper" was submitted successfully against "test collection" transaction 16509517 ("test104") and cancelled again, so TS-007 through TS-010 are not fixture-blocked. BLOCKER-EC-12000-004 (new): there is no discoverable place where the recorded Media Type can be observed, which is the assertion all five scenarios rest on. The string "Media Type" appears nowhere on the Workspace after a submission, nowhere in the Work Queue, and nowhere in the transaction History dialog (#historyDialog, columns Date / Signed / Action / Recorded By / User / IP Address / Details). More pointedly, the transaction History records no Paper Out event of any kind - its most recent entries remain "Transaction Fully Signed", "Document Added" and "Created Transaction" from 07/08/2026, despite a Paper Out having been submitted against that exact transaction minutes earlier. AC-EC-12000-016 expects Media Type as Additional Information on a "Submitted Paper Out" event, and no such event is visible in the only history view the transaction offers. This is deliberately NOT being resolved by guessing: the remaining candidate observation points named by the approved plan are the package cover page, the audit trail and the downloaded activity history report, and the cover page and activity report are only reachable through the Print/Verify action, which permanently removes source documents from the vault. Guessing wrong there is destructive and irreversible. A human must confirm where Media Type is expected to surface in 26.3, and whether the EC-12000 recording change is actually deployed to qa5 - TS-018's verbiage change is deployed, but that proves only that one part of the story shipped. Until then TS-007 through TS-010 and TS-016 stay unimplemented, and no automated pass may be asserted for them.
